newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end lower, but golds restrain fall.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end lower, but golds restrain fall.

* Toronto stocks snapped a three-day rally on Friday, but the fall was restrained by shining golds * Big losses in banking, conglomerates, consumer products * 85 million shares traded
Toronto stocks snapped a three-day winning streak on Friday, but shining golds restrained the fall on Canada's biggest stock market.
The TSE 300 Composite Index dropped 49.92 points, or 0.72 percent, to close at 6895.15. The key index earlier sank more than one percent, but recovered in later trading.
Nearly 85 million shares were traded worth C$1.4 billion.

"We've been pretty rich these last couple of months and now we're seeing a bit of a correction," one Toronto stock trader said. A buoyant gold price helped Canadian equities avoid matching a 156-point drop in the Dow Jones average.
The gold and precious metals index jumped 263 points, or 3.2 percent, as COMEX gold futures rallied on a weak U.S. dollar, bonds and stocks. COMEX October gold ended up US$4.60 at US$328.30 an ounce.
But gold stocks were overwhelmed by heavy losses in financial services, conglomerates and consumer products.

"Everbody has been worried about the steep ascent of the Dow and TSE. Profit taking was going to happen at some point and the catalyst for this was weakness in the bond markets," said Katherine Beattie, a technical analyst with MMS International.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Among the banks, Royal Bank of Canada fell 1.05 to 57.55, while Bank of Nova Scotia dropped 1.45 to 65.80.
Bank stocks have rallied recently on rating upgrades by U.S. brokerage houses.

* ATS Automation Tooling Systems Inc jumped 7 to close at 37. The stock earlier hit a 52-week high of 38 after the company announced a contract worth as much as US$375 million over the next three years.
* Placer Dome Inc was the most active gold stock, climbing 1.30 to 25.25 on 1.3 million shares.
